issues.description: The trusted drop_meta_in_place contract checks reference-count and list-membership values from an owner that is not required to describe the receiver, so those checks do not establish exclusive access to the metadata being destroyed.
issues.rationale: The complete requires block contains neither slot_own.inv()/wf() nor slot-owner-to-self identity requirements. It ties metadata_perms storage and vtable addresses to self, but the exclusive-reference-count and zero-list checks come from a separate slot_own and are not tied to self.ref_count or self.in_list. Consequently an owner for slot B can discharge these predicates while the metadata permissions refer to slot A; the stated precondition does not establish the receiver exclusivity claimed in the safety documentation. The direct child repair replaces slot_own with concrete count/list permissions and requires self.ref_count.id()==ref_count_perm.id() and self.in_list.id()==in_list_perm.id(), while retaining their value conditions. It also adds vtable initialization. This label is the identity-missing trusted-boundary contract root, not a claim of reproduced runtime memory corruption: the body is external_body and still contains unimplemented placeholders in both revisions.
